rules.effect: Rental units in buildings whose building permit issued after Dec 31, 1975 are EXEMPT from DC rent stabilization (D.C. Code § 42-3502.05(a)(2)); pre-1976 stock is presumptively covered unless another exemption applies. Newly created units in existing structures with a C of O after Jan 1, 1980 are also exempt.
rules.quote: Any rental unit in any newly constructed housing accommodation for which the building permit was issued after December 31, 1975 ... shall be exempt
rules.verification: 3-0 adversarial panel against fetched code text

rules.effect: Pre-1976 building escapes rent stabilization ONLY via the small-landlord exemption: housing accommodation of 4 or fewer rental units (aggregated across structures), owned by not more than 4 natural persons, none holding any direct or indirect interest in any other DC rental unit. An LLC or corporate owner does NOT qualify; owning any other DC rental disqualifies. Claim of exemption must be registered (RAD registration/BBL still required).
rules.quote: (3) ... any rental unit in any housing accommodation of 4 or fewer rental units, including any aggregate of 4 rental units whether within the same structure or not, provided: (A) The housing accommodation is owned by not more than 4 natural persons; (B) None of the housing providers has an interest, either directly or indirectly, in any other rental unit in the District of Columbia
rules.verification: 3-0 adversarial panel against fetched code text

rules.effect: Before selling a DC housing accommodation (or issuing a demolition/discontinuance notice to vacate), the owner must give tenants an opportunity to purchase at a bona fide offer (D.C. Code § 42-3404.02(a)). Entity-interest transfers count: selling the LLC/corporation/trust whose principal asset is the building is a 'sale' (§ 42-3404.02(c)(1)(B)(i)) — TOPA cannot be structured around. 5+ unit offers without a third-party contract trigger the tenant-organization appraisal regime (§ 42-3404.02(a-1)). Process tiers/timelines for single-family vs 2-4 unit vs 5+ live in §§ 42-3404.09-.11.
rules.verification: Verbatim quotes pulled from fetched code text; adversarial panel cut by usage limit (1 of 3 votes completed, affirmative)

rules.effect: Vacant property is taxed at Class 3 ($5.00 per $100 assessed) and blighted at Class 4 ($10.00 per $100) vs Class 1 residential $0.85 per $100 — a 6-12x carrying-cost penalty during long renovations unless a vacancy exemption is obtained.
rules.verification: OTR rate table, single primary source

rules.effect: Montgomery County rent stabilization (Bill 15-23, effective 2024) caps annual increases at CPI-U + 3%, maximum 6%. Key exemptions include buildings first occupied fewer than 23 years ago (rolling window) and small owner-occupied configurations; exact exemption list in county code — verify per deal.
rules.verification: Cap formula verified in July 15 pass (CPI+3% capped at 6%); exemption details sourced, panel cut

rules.effect: Takoma Park runs its OWN rent stabilization (City Code Ch. 6.20) on top of being inside Montgomery County: covers all rental properties of 2+ units (and individually rented condos), with NO small-building or natural-person exemption comparable to DC/PG. Allowance = 100% of CPI change; July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027 allowance published at 3.0% (corrected from an initially published 3.3%). Vacancy control reported (cap persists between tenancies) - pending confirmation.
rules.verification: City newsflash + code chapter snippet-confirmed; panels cut by usage limit

rules.effect: Permanent Rent Stabilization and Protection Act (CB-55-2024, enacted June 18 2024, effective Sept 15 2024; codified around County Code § 13-147): annual rent increases for covered units capped at the LESSER of 6.0% or CPI-U + 3% (age-restricted senior facilities: lesser of 4.5% or CPI-U). Annual allowance updates each July 1.
rules.verification: County DPIE pages; second primary (county code text) fetch in progress

rules.effect: A rental unit is EXEMPT from the PRSA if the landlord owns 5 or fewer rental units in the county AND is a natural person (or a natural person's living trust, or a decedent's trust/estate). DOMICILE FINDING: the county's FAQ attaches a domicile-in-county condition ONLY to the separate CONDOMINIUM exemption ('a condominium unit owned by one or more persons domiciled in the County'); the 5-or-fewer natural-person exemption carries NO domicile condition in the FAQ text — a Virginia-resident natural person qualifies. No affirmative exemption application is required while qualifying conditions hold; exemption lapses when conditions cease. Pending: confirmation against the county code text itself (fetch in progress) before relying on this for a domicile-sensitive purchase.
rules.verification: County FAQ pages via independent searches; CB-55 FAQ PDF (Rev. 5-14-25) + § 13-147 code text fetch in progress to upgrade to verified

rules.effect: Rental dwelling license required for non-owner-occupied rentals including 1-2 family homes (expanded 2018; Baltimore City Code Art. 13). Since Jan 1, 2019 an unlicensed landlord has NO legal right to collect rent. No rent-increase percentage cap exists, but increases are barred while housing-code violation notices citing serious defects remain unabated — directly binding on dated value-add stock; sequence is license, cure violations, then reposition.
rules.verification: Maryland People's Law Library (Maryland State Law Library); snippet-confirmed across independent queries; city code text not directly fetched

rules.effect: Virginia localities have no enabling authority to impose rent control (Dillon Rule state; no statute grants rent-regulation power). No Virginia locality operates rent control as of July 2026. Statewide VRLTA (Title 55.1, Ch. 12) governs landlord-tenant terms: security deposit capped at 2 months' rent (§ 55.1-1226), notice and disclosure duties apply. Exact statutory anchor for the preemption point being confirmed via live fetch (user-supplied cite § 55.1-1243 is being checked against the actual section text - preliminary reading: that section covers a different subject).
rules.verification: law.lis.virginia.gov fetched cleanly in July 15-16 subagent passes; precise section-level cite fetch in progress

rules.effect: Philadelphia Code § 9-811: before taking steps to evict, a landlord must enroll in the city's Eviction Diversion Program, give the tenant notice of diversion rights, and participate in reasonable good faith for at least 30 days before filing in Municipal Court. Adds a mandatory pre-filing delay to turnover of occupied units. No unit-count carve-out found in operative text (small landlords covered). Pennsylvania has no state or local rent control.
rules.quote: the landlord participates in the eviction diversion program in reasonable good faith, as defined by the City, for no less than thirty (30) days
rules.verification: 3-0 adversarial panel; statute text snippet-confirmed via independent exact-phrase searches

rules.effect: PA 22-30 (2022) made fair rent commissions MANDATORY in every CT municipality of 25,000+ (ordinance deadline July 1, 2023) — New Haven, Hartford, Bridgeport all covered. Under CGS § 7-148b commissions hold adjudicative power: investigate complaints, subpoena, hold hearings, and ORDER rent reductions for rents found harsh and unconscionable. Case-by-case rent regulation risk on post-renovation repositioning. Separately, PA 24-143 §§ 16-17 (eff. Oct 1, 2024) requires 45 days' advance written notice statewide for any rent increase; tenant non-response is not agreement.
rules.verification: OLR report language snippet-confirmed across independent queries; PDF 403-blocked to fetchers; panels cut

rules.effect: ETPA rent stabilization's qualifying vacancy analysis is restricted to buildings of 6+ units built before Jan 1, 1974 — 2-4 unit product sits OUTSIDE ETPA even in municipalities that opt in. Post-2019 HSTPA any NY municipality may opt in on a sub-5% vacancy finding (latent adoption risk), but as of July 16, 2026 HCR lists adoptions only in Nassau, Rockland, Westchester, and Ulster counties — no Capital Region (Albany/Troy) adoption.
rules.verification: HCR page sentences verbatim-confirmed via independent domain-restricted search snippets; panels cut
